about: The vocabulary of reasons for choosing a play, built from the player's own words during play. Claude tags each explained play with these codes (catalog/annotations.jsonl). A new code starts as 'proposed' and becomes 'adopted' only when the player agrees; its definition uses the player's words.

reasons.name: Uncover the most hidden
reasons.definition: My normal goal is to uncover face-down cards on the column with the most face-down cards. The overarching strategy is to uncover the card on the columns that has the most potential to reveal more cards to be played.

history.name: Uncover the most hidden
history.definition: My normal goal is to uncover face-down cards on the column with the most face-down cards.

reasons.name: Right-most playable first
reasons.definition: At the beginning of the game, I do this by selecting the right-most card that is playable.

reasons.name: Ace straight home
reasons.definition: An ace always goes straight to home since not playing it has the most downside (covering a face-down card, blocking a column from accepting a high card, preventing the next card in the home pile from being played, etc.). Moving an ace to home has only upside consequences.

reasons.name: Keep options open
reasons.definition: I don't want to make that decision prematurely. Not playing either of them until I have a king to put in the columns is an unnecessary decision that locks me into a position before I know what's coming next. Leaving them in place leaves my options open.

reasons.name: Only new plays
reasons.definition: No new play, so I'll draw. / The 7♦w-a is the only new play, so I'll play it.

reasons.name: Build the longer run
reasons.definition: When there is nothing else to consider, I play the 9 with the most run-cards on it. There may be no advantage in doing so, but I opt for continuing to build an existing longer run over starting or adding to a smaller one (all other things being equal).

reasons.name: King to an empty column
reasons.definition: Because my goal is to not use memory/card-counting, playing a king is an automatic play, similar to the reason for always playing an ace on its home pile.
